question: Do the 2025 Lake Bato survey and 2024 Baao Lake janitor-fish removal report support publishable taxonomic occurrence rows, and what does the NFRDI monitoring source add?

sourcesReviewed.citation: Mendoza, A. B. Jr., Nieves, P. M., Nolial, J. C. C., & Celestial, N. (2025). Diversity and Abundance of Fish and Mollusk Species in Lake Bato, Bicol Region, Philippines. Lux Veritatis, 11(1), 80-105.
sourcesReviewed.access: Full 26-page publisher-hosted PDF, issue listing and journal copyright page reviewed. The issue page dates Volume 11 No. 1 to April 30, 2025; the PDF imprint also says © 2020, an unresolved date/imprint discrepancy.

reportedEvidence.waterbody: Lake Bato, spanning the Bato, Camarines Sur and Libon, Albay sides.
reportedEvidence.methods: The paper reports purposive interviews with 50 fishers and fish/macroinvertebrate sampling at designated landing sites in Libon and Bato plus test fishing with local fishers using several gear types. It does not state exact specimen dates, station coordinates, voucher/accession IDs, or an event-by-taxon crosswalk.
reportedEvidence.reportedCounts: The abstract reports 17 fish, three mollusks and one freshwater shrimp, then says eight species were introduced and three native. The results instead say 10 native and 14 introduced, totaling 24 classifications for 21 reported aquatic species. These counts are unreconciled.
reportedEvidence.taxonResolution: The inventory lists named taxa, but the abundance table is a partial station-level list: six named fish taxa plus an unidentified goby, alongside four non-fish categories. The paper's claimed local name and sinarapan identity is not linked to specimen vouchers and cannot resolve the separate NFRDI tabyos identity lead.
reportedEvidence.sitePrecision: The two collection areas are described as the Libon and Bato sides, without coordinates or exact station crosswalk. Landings and test fishing are combined in the method description, so the paper does not establish which listed taxon came from which precise station or event.

qualityConcerns: The abstract's 8 introduced plus 3 native classification and the results' 10 native plus 14 introduced classification do not reconcile with the 21 total species stated in the results.
The abundance table does not enumerate all taxa in the paper's broader inventory, and unidentified gobies remain at family-level resolution.
The source describes Channa striata as introduced/farmed in its table; do not propagate origin labels without independent taxonomic and biogeographic review.
Sampling dates, specimen vouchers, sequence accessions and catch-event links are absent; do not infer current presence, abundance or station coordinates.
The reported diversity statistics are source claims only, not recalculated from raw data.
sourcesReviewed.reuse: The publisher's copyright page says article copyright remains with authors and publisher and that citation/printing/photocopying is subject to Fair Use. No item-specific open-data license or permission for reproducing tables or derived app records was found. This review retains a short attributed assessment only.

sourcesReviewed.citation: BFAR Region V. (2024, June 8). Fishers Retrieve Invasive Species in Baao Lake, Gets Incentive as Part of the BASIL Program.
sourcesReviewed.access: Full official BFAR Region V page retrieved and reviewed. It reports that three fisherfolk collectively removed 85 kg of locally named janitor fish from Baao Lake; BFAR released incentives on June 5, 2024. No biological sample dataset or exact capture site was provided.

reportedEvidence.waterbody: Baao Lake, Camarines Sur, as named in the BFAR page.
reportedEvidence.evidenceType: Agency-reported invasive-fish removal and incentive activity under BASIL, not a biological survey or scientific-name occurrence event.
reportedEvidence.taxonAsReported: Janitor fish; the page does not give a scientific name, specimen identifier, image-based determination, count of individuals or length/weight protocol.
reportedEvidence.dateAndLocationPrecision: The article is posted June 8, 2024 and says the incentive release occurred June 5, 2024. It does not provide the removal date, shoreline/station, coordinates or a precise catch-event crosswalk.

interpretationLimits: The common name does not by itself establish a scientific species identity or unique taxon record.
The reported 85 kg is a community removal quantity, not lake abundance, catch rate or species-composition evidence.
Do not turn this management report into a species occurrence row, invasive-status assertion, current distribution claim or fishing instruction.
sourcesReviewed.reuse: No item-specific content reuse terms were identified on the reviewed page. Retain attribution and the short source claim only; no photo, table or full text was copied.

sourcesReviewed.citation: DA-NFRDI. (2025). Reassessing the catch: Lake Bato's fisheries in focus. Fisearch, 7(2), 24-25.
sourcesReviewed.access: The official NFRDI repository metadata and full two-page newsletter article were reviewed and matched against the already-registered NFRDI feature page. It describes 2025-2026 monitoring with four enumerators at eight landing sites and preliminary tabyos morphology/genetics. It is the same communication, not an independent second assessment.

reportedEvidence.identityLead: The NFRDI feature calls the local name tabyos ambiguous and describes Gobiopterus luzonensis batonensis as a likely preliminary identification, conditional on confirmation. No diagnostic voucher list or sequence accessions are supplied in the newsletter.
reportedEvidence.inventoryAvailability: The two-page piece contains no full taxon checklist, station-by-taxon table, specimen counts or machine-readable catch dataset.
reportedEvidence.relationshipTo2026Summary: The 2026 NFRDI summary later reports 31 species and 19 introduced in a two-year Lake Bato assessment but supplies no full list or voucher audit. Keep this as program-level context; do not merge the counts with the 2025 journal paper or treat separate summaries as independent surveys.

sourcesReviewed.reuse: No item-specific reuse license was verified. Repository accessibility and official-agency publication are not blanket permission to reuse content or data.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Corpuz, M. N. C., Paller, V. G. V., & Ocampo, P. P. (2015). Ichthyofaunal Survey in Selected Freshwater Habitats in Camarines Sur, Philippines. Asian Journal of Biodiversity, 6(1).
sourcesReviewed.access: The already-reviewed 2010 five-habitat survey is retained as historical context: its published site table includes Lake Bato and Lake Baao-Bula, but it does not establish current occurrences. It reports no voucher crosswalk that links its records to the newer Bato claims.
sourcesReviewed.reuse: No item-specific reuse license or permission was verified in the earlier review. No species table is reproduced here.

crossSourceAssessment.lakeBato: The 2010 five-habitat survey, 2025 Lux Veritatis sample/inventory paper, NFRDI monitoring newsletter and 2026 NFRDI results summary describe separate or program-linked evidence with no shared event/specimen/voucher crosswalk. The 2025 paper's unresolved counts and identity claims cannot settle the historical sinarapan/tabyos question.
crossSourceAssessment.baaoBula: The older 2010 survey remains the only reviewed taxon-by-lake table lead in this batch. The 2024 BFAR removal story adds a recent management-action report under the common name janitor fish, not a scientific-name checklist. Lake Baao/Bula is separately named in EMB's classified-water-body registry, which is water-quality context rather than fish data.
crossSourceAssessment.habitatSeparation: Lake Bato, Lake Baao-Bula, tributary rivers and Bicol River estuarine reaches remain distinct habitat units. Do not transfer an occurrence between a lake, its outlet, river reaches, landing sites or markets without a specimen/catch-site link.
crossSourceAssessment.appReadiness: Research leads only. None of the newly reviewed material supplies a rights-cleared, complete, dated, taxonomically audited, station-by-event species dataset ready for public app use.

disposition.reason: The 2025 paper lacks exact dates, station/event and voucher crosswalks and contains incompatible totals/origin classifications; BFAR's Baao Lake removal record uses an unidentified common name and has no catch site or specimen link. Rights for both new source items are unresolved.

nextAction: Continue the Bicol inland-water sweep with Lake Buhi and the smaller crater lakes (Danao, Manapao, Katugday and Makuao), then pursue current primary datasets for Lake Bato/Baao-Bula and connected streams. Keep official catch-removal reports separate from biological surveys; do not mark Bicol complete.

sources.supports: Full 2025 Lake Bato paper, stated sampling approach, inventory/table claims, unresolved count and origin-classification conflicts, and absence of exact specimen dates/voucher crosswalk.
Publisher issue metadata, authors and publication date for Lux Veritatis volume 11 no. 1.
